I went to a restaurant recently that had all the calories on the menu, up front and in your face. And it was amazing. My stomach was feeling the burger with cheese and bacon with an egg on top. I didn't care that it cost $18 from my wallet, but when I saw that it was 1600 calories (more if I went with fries instead of salad), then I changed my mind and went with something more sensible. And I realized that while the price is the cost to your wallet, the calorie count is the cost to your weight / health.

Restaurants are already required to make calorie count available to you if you ask for it, but nobody wants to be that turd holding up the line, and there's an implied admission of fatness that makes it embarrassing. Plus, when you get it it's in a giant chart that you have to cross-reference with the menu because one is alphabetical and the other is ordered by food type.

But having it right there on the menu was so helpful. And it's not like I saw the high-calorie burger and said, "Fuck this restaurant, I'm going home." I just picked something else. And in this case, it happened to be more expensive, too.
The world would be thinner if calories were written in the same size as the price on the menu.

And a function that replaces cd mv and mkdir, except in the case when you want to make a directory and not go into it. This is for dribbling files around. It's not another command to remeber because it replaces 90% of use cases for the others.

This replaces:
mv cd
mkdir cd
mkdir mv cd
cd
and mkdir cd mkdir cd mkdir cd mkdir cd ../../../../../ mv *.ext ////////// cd ////////// (not that you would ever do it that way.) (I know you have though.)

drib () {
 for last; do true; done
 mkdir -p "$last"
 if [ "$#" -ge 2 ]; then
 mv "$@"
 fi
 cd "$last"
}

In fact because you only ever call cd with one argument you might as well call this one cd, then just remember that it will create a directrory if you need it and move files into it if you list more than one. cd - would break though.
